changelog: Replace C3 to address the primary finding by describing what a GOOD cut around predicates looks like (include predicate + essential complements; allow cut only when continuation is optional or parenthetical).
Replace C5 to explicitly treat post‑nominal modifiers and complements as part of the noun when they determine reference, matching the second finding.
Paraphrase C8 shorter to free space while keeping its guidance about translation guessing and cohesion.
Paraphrased C8 to shorten guidance about translation guessing and cohesion, freeing space for a focused rule.

Inserted a new Core Principle after C5 that forbids cutting a head noun or name away from post‑nominal modifiers/complements that determine reference or truth conditions (addresses the primary finding).
Insert a narrow, surface-form rule after C2 to forbid cuts that split a main verb from its essential complement (addresses the primary finding about predicate–argument separation).

Insert a narrow surface-form rule after C5 forbidding cuts that separate a head noun or proper name from immediately following post‑nominal material that visibly completes or identifies that noun (addresses the primary finding).

Replace E1..E4 (handwritten examples) with four measured, labeled examples that illustrate predicate–complement splits and related post‑nominal/complement hazards (addresses the primary finding that the prompt underrates cuts separating verbs from essential complements).

Selected examples en_us_1116, en_us_936, en_us_113, en_us_164 because each is a measured case where splitting a predicate from its core argument or separating noun from essential post‑nominal material produced large cohesion/contra loss.
Replace E1 with measured example en_us_1617: gives a real case with a post‑nominal 'which' clause to teach not cutting before modifiers that determine a noun.
Replace E2 with measured example en_us_105: gives a real case with a 'from which' PP that completes a noun and so should not be separated by a cut.
Delete E3 (handwritten example) to free space and reduce prompt length.
Delete E4 (handwritten example) to free space and reduce prompt length.

Insert after C2 a concise rule describing what a GOOD cut around predicates looks like: keep the main verb with its essential complements and allow cuts only when the continuation is optional or parenthetical — addresses the primary finding without a blanket ban.

Insert a narrow surface-form rule after C5 forbidding cuts that separate a head noun or proper name from immediately following post‑nominal material (relative pronoun, preposition+'which', or appositive comma). This targets the primary finding about post‑nominal modifiers.
